options.text: the running costs of the power station
a coal-fired power station

the supply curve moved to the left

questions.questionText:
A government subsidises the production of pineapples.
This is likely to

options.text: increase the price of pineapples
raise the costs of supplying pineapples
raise revenue for the government

questions.questionText: What indicates the existence of external costs in an economy?

options.text: An international trade deficit has caused the country to be in debt.
National companies have borrowed from foreign investors.
Private costs of production are less than social costs.
Private costs of production are more than social benefits.

questions.questionText: What might be a disadvantage to a trade union when arguing for an increase in its members’ pay?

options.text: an increase in imports of a cheaper, similar product
the closure of a local training college resulting in fewer potential workers
the development of a new and profitable brand of the company’s product
the development of new techniques that increase productivity

questions.questionText:
What shows the correct examples of income and wealth?
income wealth

options.text: dividends from shares wages
rent from a house overtime payments
overtime payments wages
wages house

questions.questionText:
Nazmin Uddin works in a local office as a secretary three days a week. She lives with her parents
in a small apartment.
Meer Ali owns a successful fitness centre that employs about twenty people. He owns a large
house.
Which is most likely to be correct?

options.text: Nazmin spends a smaller proportion of her income than Meer.
Nazmin saves most of her income.
Nazmin would find it easier than Meer to borrow money.
Nazmin has a lower disposable income than Meer.

questions.questionText:
A survey of managers in the USA revealed that most businessmen feel that a company’s
responsibility is ‘to serve the interests of owners, employees, customers and the public’.
The idea of profit maximisation, in contrast, implies that a company’s main responsibility should
be to the

options.text: customers
employees
owners
public

questions.questionText:
Some agricultural co-operatives have changed from labour-intensive to capital-intensive methods
of production.
What might be a cause of this change?

options.text: Average productivity of agricultural workers has increased.
Farming equipment has become more efficient.
People are eating less food for health reasons.
Some agricultural land has been sold for housing.

questions.questionText:
A firm has fixed costs of $200 for its daily output. The table shows its daily total variable costs.
output (units) 1 2 3 4
total variable costs ($) 300 400 700 800
What can be concluded about the firm’s average total cost?

options.text: it falls continuously
it is highest at output 4 units
it is lowest at output 4 units
it rises continuously

questions.questionText:
A government decides to sell the monopoly supply of gas to households to a private firm.
How could the government protect the interests of households after selling a large company to
the private sector?

options.text: by excluding all competition from foreign companies
by imposing a tax on excess profits
by introducing a quota system for imports of gas
by removing price controls on gas

questions.questionText:
In 2015, 70000 extra people lost their jobs but total employment rose by 75000. What could
explain this?

options.text: Some people may have emigrated.
Some people may have gone back to education.
Some people may have re-entered the labour force.
Some people may have retired early.

incomes

questions.questionText:
Why is nominal Gross Domestic Product not a good measure to compare the standard of living in
a country between two years?

options.text: It does not account for inflation.
It does not allow for savings.
It does not include government expenditure.
It only compares export prices with import prices.

questions.questionText:
In 2010 there was an increase in net emigration from Ireland.
What is most likely to have caused this increase?

options.text: a decrease in job security abroad
a decrease in wage rates abroad
an increase in Ireland’s real GDP
an increase in unemployment in Ireland

questions.questionText:
Some goods take a greater percentage of a typical household’s total spending than others.
How is this accounted for in the construction of a Retail Price Index?

options.text: by deducting the goods and services
by giving a weight to the goods
by taking an average of price fluctuations during a year
by using the price elasticity of demand for the goods

questions.questionText: Which outcome is least likely to be found with greater economic development?

options.text: A greater percentage of the population are highly educated.
A greater percentage of the population are homeowners.
A greater percentage of the population are old.
A greater percentage of the population are very poor.

questions.questionText:
A government introduces state benefits for the unemployed and increases the top rate of income
tax to pay for the benefits.
What effect will these changes have on poverty and the tax system?
poverty tax system

options.text: increase make it more progressive
increase make it more regressive
reduce make it more progressive
reduce make it more regressive

questions.questionText: What encourages international specialisation?

options.text: a foreign exchange shortage
diseconomies of scale
free trade
quotas

questions.questionText:
A Japanese car manufacturer decided to produce its cars in a factory in Europe.
What would not be a reason why they might have chosen to do this?

options.text: cheaper wage costs in Europe
the availability of raw materials
to gain external economies from skilled labour in Europe
to increase Japanese self-sufficiency

questions.questionText:
A government removed the quota on goods imported into the country.
What is the most likely result of this?

options.text: a decrease in demand for domestic production
a decrease in domestic unemployment
a decrease in exports
a decrease in the balance of trade deficit
